title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

claims.text: Every Microsoft Fabric tenant is provisioned with exactly one OneLake; tenants cannot create additional OneLake instances or delete the existing one, and no separate storage resources need to be provisioned or managed.

OneLake is layered on Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 and exposes the same ADLS Gen2 APIs and SDKs, so existing ADLS-aware applications such as Azure Databricks can read and write OneLake data without code changes.

OneLake's addressing model virtualizes the whole tenant as one giant ADLS storage account: each Fabric workspace surfaces as a container in that account, and each data item surfaces as a folder inside its workspace container.
All Fabric data items, including lakehouses and warehouses, automatically persist their tabular data in OneLake using the open Delta Parquet format, regardless of which engine wrote the data.

The one-copy design lets multiple Fabric engines (T-SQL, Apache Spark, Analysis Services, and others) operate over the same physical Delta Parquet data, so teams do not duplicate datasets per engine or get locked into the engine that first loaded the data.

Direct Lake mode in the Analysis Services engine lets Power BI semantic models read Delta Parquet data straight from OneLake, delivering import-mode speed without maintaining a copied dataset, alongside the existing import and DirectQuery modes.

Governance in OneLake is hierarchical: tenant-level security, compliance, and data-management policies automatically cover any data landing in OneLake, while workspaces distribute ownership and access policies, with each workspace attached to a capacity in a specific region and billed separately.

OneLake shortcuts are references to data held in other locations, within the same workspace, across workspaces, or outside OneLake in stores like ADLS, Amazon S3, or Dataverse, and they make remote files and folders appear as if stored locally, enabling virtual data products without duplication.

Standing up separate physical data lakes per business group, a common pre-OneLake practice, is an antipattern in Fabric because it recreates resource-management overhead and data duplication that the single tenant-wide OneLake with workspaces and shortcuts is designed to eliminate.
OneLake soft delete retains deleted files for seven days, and soft-deleted files can be restored with Azure Storage Explorer or PowerShell, providing protection against accidental deletion.

For resilience, OneLake stores data on zone-redundant storage (ZRS) where the region supports it, and capacities can additionally enable business continuity and disaster recovery (BCDR) to replicate data to a secondary geographic region.
OneLake file explorer for Windows lets users browse all workspaces and data items and upload, download, or edit files from the desktop, making the data lake usable by non-technical business users.
